Inter's greatest manager of all time? Our pick: José Mourinho.
https://www.nerazzurridaily.com/go/yt/?v=debate4 — the Italian Inter press in English every morning, free

THE DEBATE — a weekly fan-made argument, not the news.

Helenio Herrera (1960–68, 1973–74): 7 trophies — Scudetti 1963, 1965, 1966; European Cups 1964 and 1965; Intercontinental Cups 1964 and 1965. The Grande Inter.
Giovanni Trapattoni (1986–91): Scudetto 1988–89 with a record 58 points; Supercoppa 1989; UEFA Cup 1991.
Roberto Mancini (2004–08, 2014–16): 7 trophies — Scudetti 2005–06 (awarded after Calciopoli), 2006–07 and 2007–08; Coppa Italia 2005 and 2006; Supercoppa 2005 and 2006; a record 97 points in 2006–07.
José Mourinho (2008–10): 5 trophies — Scudetti 2008–09 and 2009–10; Coppa Italia 2010; Supercoppa 2008; Champions League 2010, the only treble by an Italian club; 68 wins in 108 games.
Antonio Conte (2019–21): Scudetto 2020–21; Europa League final 2020.
Simone Inzaghi (2021–25): 6 trophies — Scudetto 2023–24; Coppa Italia 2022 and 2023; Supercoppa 2021, 2022 and 2023; Champions League finals 2023 and 2025.

Sources: inter.it (manager archive and club history), uefa.com, Wikipedia (English).
Fan-made — not affiliated with FC Internazionale Milano.

#Inter #ForzaInter #Mourinho #Herrera #SerieA #Shorts

# THE DEBATE No. 4 — Inter's greatest manager? (D04) — research, Oct 14, 2026

Everything below was read this session. Authority order: inter.it > uefa.com > Wikipedia > press.

## Helenio Herrera (Inter 1960–68; brief return 1973–74)
- inter.it manager archive (career table, every season): Scudetto 1962/63, 1964/65, 1965/66; "UEFA Champions League" (European Cup) winners 1963/64 and 1964/65; Intercontinental Cup winners 1964/65 and 1965/66; Coppa Italia final 1964/65; European Cup final 1966/67 (lost). Total row W 205 D 93 L 68 (= 366 matches, both spells). https://www.inter.it/en/archivio_allenatore/28/Herrera%20Helenio%20Herrera
- inter.it, "Helenio Herrera, 110 years since his birth": three league titles ('63, '65, '66), two Champions Cups ('64, '65), two Intercontinental Cups — "seven major trophies"; built the "Grande Inter"; "The Wizard". https://www.inter.it/en/news/2020-04-10-110-years-since-herreras-birth
- inter.it, "27 May, the date of two European Cups for Inter": May 27, 1964, Vienna, Inter 3–1 Real Madrid (Mazzola 2, Milani); May 27, 1965, San Siro, Inter 1–0 Benfica (Jair). https://www.inter.it/en/news/2020-05-27-27-may-inter-european-cups-1964-and-1965
- uefa.com, "The greatest teams of all time: Inter 1962–67": Scudetti 1962/63, 1964/65, 1965/66; European Cups 1964 and 1965; lost the 1967 final to Celtic; catenaccio, Picchi libero, Facchetti attacking full-back. https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0253-0d7ff54821f7-e2055930d1e0-1000--the-greatest-teams-of-all-time-inter-1962-67
- Wikipedia (en), Helenio Herrera: spells July 9, 1960 – June 30, 1968 and July 19, 1973 – Feb 5, 1974; honours as above; first-spell record 343 P 194 W 86 D 63 L. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helenio_Herrera
- Wikipedia (en), List of Inter Milan managers: Herrera 9 seasons, 360 P 204 W 91 D 65 L, 56.67%; 7 trophies; "Herrera and Mancini are the most successful managers in terms of number of trophies won"; "longest-serving manager with nine seasons, eight of which were consecutive". https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Inter_Milan_managers
- DISCREPANCY: matches/wins — inter.it 366 (205-93-68) vs Wikipedia 360 (204-91-65). Win % therefore NOT shown on screen. Trophy counts agree everywhere (7).
- First European Cup came in his 4th season (1960/61 → 1963/64); 7 trophies in the 8-season first spell.

## José Mourinho (Inter June 2, 2008 – May 28, 2010)
- inter.it manager archive: 2008/09 Serie A Scudetto, Supercoppa Italiana winners; 2009/10 Serie A Scudetto, Champions League winners, Coppa Italia winners; Total W 68 D 25 L 15 (= 108 matches, 63.0%). https://www.inter.it/en/archivio_allenatore/57/Mourinho%20Jos%C3%A9%20Mourinho
- Wikipedia (en), List of Inter Milan managers: 2 seasons, 108 P 68 W 25 D 15 L, 62.96%, 5 trophies (SA 2, CI 1, SCI 1, UCL 1). AGREES with inter.it. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Inter_Milan_managers
- Wikipedia (en), 2009–10 Inter Milan season: Serie A won with 82 points (24-10-4), decided on the final matchday May 16, 2010; Champions League final May 22, 2010, Inter 2–0 Bayern Munich, Milito both goals, Man of the Match; "first and only Italian club" to win the treble, sixth European club; "Inter's first European Cup since 1965 and third overall". https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Inter_Milan_season
- Wikipedia (en), José Mourinho: appointed June 2, 2008; Supercoppa 2008 (Roma, penalties); Serie A 2008–09 by 10 points; Coppa Italia final May 5, 2010, 1–0 Roma; Champions League May 22, 2010; left for Real Madrid, release agreed May 28, 2010. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Mourinho
- beIN Sports, "On this day – Inter make it a treble": final at the Santiago Bernabéu, Madrid, 2–0, Milito both goals; resigned six days later for Real Madrid. https://www.beinsports.com/en-mena/football/uefa-champions-league/articles/on-this-day-inter-make-it-a-treble
- Derived: 1965 → 2010 = 45 years between European Cups. Trophies per season 5/2 = 2.5.

## Giovanni Trapattoni (Inter July 1, 1986 – June 30, 1991)
- inter.it, "Trap at 80": 1988/89 Scudetto, "58 points from 68 were won", clinched v Napoli with five games left; Supercoppa Italiana 1989; UEFA Cup 1991 (beat Roma over two legs). https://www.inter.it/en/news/2019-03-17-trap-at-80-best-wishes-from-all-at-inter
- Wikipedia (en), Giovanni Trapattoni: honours Serie A 1988–89, Supercoppa 1989, UEFA Cup 1990–91; record 233 P 124 W 65 D 44 L. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giovanni_Trapattoni
- DISCREPANCY: managers list says 230 P 126 W 59 D 45 L. Match totals NOT shown on screen; only the three trophies and the 58 points (inter.it).

## Roberto Mancini (Inter July 7, 2004 – May 29, 2008; Nov 14, 2014 – Aug 8, 2016)
- Wikipedia (en), Roberto Mancini: Serie A 2005–06 (handed to Inter after Calciopoli), 2006–07, 2007–08; Coppa Italia 2004–05, 2005–06; Supercoppa 2005, 2006; 2006–07: record 17 consecutive Serie A wins and a record 97 points; records 226 P 140 W 60 D 26 L (first spell), 77 P 36 W 18 D 23 L (second). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Mancini
- Wikipedia (en), List of Inter Milan managers: 303 P 176 W 78 D 49 L, 58.08%; SA 3, CI 2, SCI 2 (= 7 trophies); co-most-successful with Herrera by trophy count. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Inter_Milan_managers

## Antonio Conte (Inter May 31, 2019 – May 26, 2021)
- Wikipedia (en), Antonio Conte: Serie A 2020–21 ("champions for the first time in eleven years"); Europa League final Aug 21, 2020, Cologne, lost 3–2 to Sevilla; record 102 P 64 W 23 D 15 L, 62.75%. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Conte (managers list agrees: 102/64/23/15)

## Simone Inzaghi (Inter July 1, 2021 – June 3, 2025)
- inter.it manager archive (career table): Serie A 2023/24 1st; Coppa Italia 2021/22 and 2022/23 winners (1); Supercoppa 2021/22, 2022/23, 2023/24 winners (1); Champions League 2022/23 and 2024/25 "2nd" (finals); total 141 W 41 D 35 L. https://www.inter.it/it/archivio_allenatore/72
- Wikipedia (en), Simone Inzaghi: Serie A 2023–24 (won April 22, 2024, 2–1 in the derby — the 20th title per the cited headline); Coppa Italia 2021–22, 2022–23; Supercoppa 2021, 2022, 2023; Champions League runner-up 2022–23 (0–1 Manchester City) and 2024–25 (0–5 PSG); 217 P 141 W, 64.98%. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simone_Inzaghi
- Managers list: 4 seasons, 217 P 141 W 41 D 35 L, 6 trophies. AGREES.

## The pick and the fight
- Pick: Mourinho — 5 trophies in 2 seasons (2.5 per season, the best rate of the six), the only treble by an Italian club, and the European Cup Inter had waited 45 years for.
- Counter: Herrera — 7 trophies (joint most with Mancini), 2 European Cups back-to-back, 2 Intercontinental Cups, the Grande Inter; longest-serving.
- Versus rows (all undisputed): Trophies 5–7 (Herrera); European Cups 1–2 (Herrera); Trebles 1–0 (Mourinho); Seasons needed 2–8 (Mourinho: the first-spell 8 seasons held all 7 trophies).
- Not shown on screen: Herrera and Trapattoni match totals and win % (sources disagree).
